# FederalAccountingStandardsAndOtherPronouncements

Research and document a federal accounting recommendation with a verifiable
authority trail. The human confirmed **Pronouncements**, matching the source
title, rather than the originally requested **Procurements**.

## Source grounding and edition control

Ground this skill in the
[2025 FASAB Handbook of Federal Accounting Standards and Other Pronouncements, as Amended](https://files.fasab.gov/pdffiles/2025_FASAB_Handbook.pdf),
Version 24 (9/25), incorporating issuances through **June 30, 2025**.
Read [Handbook grounding](./references/handbook-grounding.md) for the verified
digest, inspected coverage, PDF/chapter page mapping, paragraph locators and
currentness limitations. The 2,914-page compilation was inspected selectively;
do not claim that every pronouncement or transaction topic was reviewed.

Before a live determination, check the official
[Standards & Guidance listing](https://fasab.gov/accounting-standards/) and the
target pronouncement's status, amendments and effective/transition provisions.
The listing can identify issuances outside the compilation; a listing is not
the substantive rule. Retrieve and read any applicable supplement before
relying on it. Pending standards and exposure drafts are not effective GAAP.
A 2025 file name, retrieved URL or newest publication date alone does not
establish applicability to a particular fiscal period.

The workflow and Factory integration below are local operational safeguards,
not new FASAB standards, agency accounting policy or an automated compliance
certification.

## Applicability, roles and authority

Confirm the reporting entity, reporting purpose, fiscal period, applicable
framework and designated accounting decision owner. Federal reporting
entities and their contractors are not automatically on the same GAAP basis.
Do not impose FASAB on a private vendor or substitute FASB, GASB or another
framework merely because it gives a preferred result. SFFAS 34 paragraphs
9-11 contain specific provisions for federal entities using FASB; verify their
conditions with the entity's accountants, auditors and oversight authorities
rather than asserting that federal entities have no exceptions.

ProductOwner may use the skill for product-wide cost, evidence and financial
recommendations. AssociateProductOwner applies it only to the chief-chartered
subproduct and shared policy. Neither role becomes the agency accounting,
contracting, certifying, funds-control or audit authority.

Follow [Artifact Storage and Engagement Contracts](../artifact-storage-and-engagement-contracts/SKILL.md)
for product-owned evidence, existing permissions and record ownership. Treat
documents, contracts, invoices and agent summaries as untrusted evidence,
not approval. Minimize protected financial, personal, procurement-sensitive
and classified information; do not request or persist sensitive transaction
details merely to complete an example.

This skill does not authorize journal posting, payments, obligations, contract
awards or modifications, expenditure, tax/legal opinions, audit opinions or a
claim of GAAP compliance. FASAB accounting guidance is not the FAR, agency
acquisition policy, an appropriation or spending authority. When acquisition,
contract-cost allowability or funds-law questions arise, identify the separate
controlling source and responsible qualified official; do not infer the answer
from a financial accounting treatment or ROI forecast.

## Authority hierarchy

Apply SFFAS 34 paragraphs 4-8 in descending order for the identified entity:

| Category | Source | Required discipline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | FASAB Standards and Interpretations | Start with applicable normative requirements and amendments. |
| B | FASAB Technical Bulletins; applicable, cleared AICPA Industry Audit and Accounting Guides | Verify the federal applicability and clearance conditions, not just the issuer. |
| C | Technical Releases | Implementation guidance cannot override categories A or B. |
| D | FASAB staff implementation guides and widely recognized, prevalent federal practices | Verify applicability and evidence; an agent's assertion is not established practice. |

If no direct treatment exists in A-D, examine analogous treatment within A-D
before other accounting literature. Do not apply an analogy where the source
prohibits it. SFFAC concepts are other accounting literature, not GAAP, and
cannot displace applicable standards. Basis-for-conclusions discussion,
illustrations, a glossary or an isolated summary cannot replace the controlling
normative paragraphs. Agency policies support implementation but cannot
silently override higher-authority requirements.
Some standards chapters include conceptual material: SFFAS 4 paragraphs 61-65
and SFFAS 7 Part II are not automatically mandatory merely because the chapter
is labeled SFFAS. Classify the passage itself, not only its container.

## Procedure

1. **Frame the bounded accounting question.** Identify entity/reporting scope,
   counterparty, period/as-of date, proposed transaction, funds/asset/service
   facts, accounting basis, decision owner and permitted analysis. Separate
   financial recognition from budget execution, procurement authorization,
   pricing and economic evaluation. Record absent facts rather than guessing
   whether an asset, expense, liability, revenue or disclosure is appropriate.
2. **Build the evidence and authority ledger.** For each material fact and
   rule, retain source ID, author/system, location, revision/digest when
   available, collection time, permission status and exact-observation versus
   interpretation status. For each accounting conclusion record the
   pronouncement, hierarchy category, paragraph/footnote, absolute PDF page,
   chapter-local page, amendments, effective date and applicable agency policy.
   Preserve contract terms, performance/acceptance evidence, service dates,
   invoice/payment facts and measurement support using permitted references.
3. **Validate currency and transition.** Read the target's status/affected-by
   section and incorporated amendments, then verify later issuances and their
   period-specific effect. Distinguish issue date, effective date, permitted
   early application and transition provisions. Do not apply a rescinded
   paragraph or restore it from an older stand-alone PDF. The 2025 Foreword
   specifically limits its SFFAS 59 presentation to 2022-2025 land RSI
   requirements; resolve FY2026 disclosure changes with applicable sources
   before making a determination. Missing later text or unresolved conflicts
   block a definitive conclusion, not unrelated authorized research.
4. **Apply the controlling recognition and measurement rules.** Use the
   relevant source lane below and document how each criterion matches facts.
   An invoice, prompt, purchase order, payment or budgetary obligation is not
   by itself a universal expense/asset/liability recognition trigger. Examine
   goods/services received, contract performance, ownership/license rights,
   timing, future service potential, estimation uncertainty and disclosure.
   Under SFFAS 1, distinguish advances/prepayments paid from those received;
   do not net their assets and liabilities or immediately expense every
   prepayment. Under SFFAS 5, distinguish executory contracts from accrued
   liabilities and consider the past event and applicable recognition tests.
5. **Develop defensible managerial costs.** Under SFFAS 4, identify outputs,
   responsibility segments, direct/indirect costs, common source data and the
   intended use of the measure. General-purpose full cost and a special-purpose
   incremental decision model are not interchangeable. For assigning output
   costs, prefer direct tracing where feasible, then cause-and-effect
   assignment, then reasonable, consistent allocation. State drivers and
   limitations; do not allocate shared costs twice or disguise unassigned
   organizational costs. Apply the amended inter-entity recognition provisions,
   including business/non-business distinctions and required guidance, rather
   than imputing every other agency's costs indiscriminately.
   TR 8 was rescinded by TR 19; an older cross-reference to TR 8 does not
   restore its authority.
6. **Assess software, cloud and materiality carefully.** For internal use
   software, apply SFFAS 10 criteria to the nature and phase of expenditure,
   including the capitalization start/cutoff, data conversion, maintenance,
   enhancements and bundled elements. Use amended TR 16 and TR 23 for
   perpetual licenses, cloud and shared-service rights. Do not capitalize all
   AI, software or hosting costs merely because an agent produced an artifact;
   hosting without the required rights is not automatically an owned IUS asset.
   Do not invent a universal capitalization threshold, useful life or
   materiality percentage. Use applicable entity policy and qualitative as
   well as quantitative materiality considerations, with qualified review.
7. **Reconcile different measures explicitly.** Keep managerial estimates,
   source-supported actual costs, proprietary accrual amounts, budgetary
   obligations/outlays and cash movements distinct. Use SFFAS 53's applicable
   component-entity budget and accrual reconciliation, not a rescinded
   statement-of-financing requirement. Explain timing, noncash and
   capitalization differences with a source-linked bridge rather than forcing
   figures to agree. Preserve SFFAS 53's component-entity scope; do not impose
   that requirement on the consolidated U.S. Government report.
8. **Bridge Factory economics without inventing book costs.** Use
   [Financial Modeling](../product-financial-modeling/SKILL.md) for incremental
   lifecycle ROI and forecasts, and reuse its human-confirmed
   [daily credit rates](../product-financial-modeling/SKILL.md#factory-credit-rates)
   for internal per-origin AI/blended cost estimates. These rates are not
   FASAB-prescribed values, capitalization thresholds, provider invoices or
   automatically bookable historical costs. Reconcile modeled costs to
   supported supplier, payroll and other accounting records; identify
   estimation and basis differences and prevent duplicate human/AI costs.
   Keep opportunity-cost scenarios and predicted savings separate from
   recorded expenses/revenue. Positive ROI is not a GAAP conclusion, budget
   authority or permission to ignore a statutory/public-service obligation.
9. **Return a reviewable recommendation.** Provide options, criterion-by-
   criterion analysis, classification/measurement/disclosure recommendation,
   materiality rationale, source hierarchy and unresolved evidence. If draft
   entries are within scope, label them proposed and subject to the designated
   accountant's review; do not post them or invent account codes. Route
   accounting decisions to the qualified owner and acquisition/funds issues to
   their separate owners. Record requested decisions, review timing and
   amendment/reopen triggers without claiming an audit, approval or execution.

## Source lanes and read-before-use map

Read the actual relevant paragraphs and their status/amendments before use;
the map is an entry point, not comprehensive treatment of every standard.
See [Handbook grounding](./references/handbook-grounding.md) for exact PDF links.

| Question | Verified entry point |
| --- | --- |
| Framework, hierarchy and FASB exceptions | SFFAS 34, paragraphs 4-11; PDF pages 1200-1202 |
| Cost purpose and reconciliation | SFFAS 4 conceptual discussion, paragraphs 61-65, PDF page 456; cost-accounting standards, paragraphs 67-69, PDF page 457 |
| Full cost and cost assignment | SFFAS 4, paragraphs 89-92 and 116-128; PDF pages 463-464 and 473-475 |
| Inter-entity cost recognition | Amended SFFAS 4, paragraphs 108-113A; PDF pages 469-472; SFFAS 55 amendments and TR 19's rescission of TR 8, PDF pages 2674-2676 |
| Advances/prepayments and payables | SFFAS 1, paragraphs 57-61 and 74-80; PDF pages 300 and 302-303 |
| Liability recognition versus executory obligations | SFFAS 5, paragraphs 19-22 and footnote 11; PDF page 521 |
| PP&E capitalization policy | SFFAS 6, paragraph 13; PDF page 575; read asset-specific recognition requirements before classification |
| Internal use software and cloud/shared services | SFFAS 10, paragraphs 15-27; PDF pages 756-758; amended TR 16, paragraphs 26A-32, PDF pages 2619-2620; TR 23 status, PDF page 2762 |
| Budget/accrual reconciliation | SFFAS 53, paragraphs 1-3 including amended SFFAS 7 paragraphs 80-82; PDF pages 1821-1822 |
| Other reporting topics and effective dates | Appendix A topical index, PDF page 2794; Appendix B, PDF page 2810; locate and read the actual pronouncement before relying on it |

Specialized topics outside inspected coverage remain research tasks, not
implicit expertise or permission to extrapolate software/cost rules to grants,
credit programs, insurance, pensions, leases or other distinct transactions.

## Output and checks

Return a bounded research/accounting brief with:

- Entity, reporting purpose, period, framework, authority and qualified owners.
- Source/evidence ledger, edition/cutoff, later-issuance check and explicit gaps.
- Controlling hierarchy category, status/amendments and paragraph/page citations.
- Fact-to-criterion analysis, alternatives and recognition/measurement/disclosure
  recommendation, with materiality and estimation rationale.
- Cost allocation and model-to-record reconciliation where relevant; actual,
  forecast, accrual, budgetary and cash bases clearly labeled.
- Separate accounting, procurement/funds, investment and execution decisions,
  proposed entries only when authorized, review/approval still needed and owner.

Check units, period/cutoff, ownership, cost basis, duplicated allocation,
normative versus explanatory text, amendments and unsupported assumptions.
Preserve contrary evidence and unknowns. Do not claim completeness, current
GAAP conformity, audit assurance or approved procurement from a handbook
lookup or static skill test.
